# zenmeta

Shared metadata implementation for image codecs, using zencodec's interchange
types. Metadata operations do not require zenpipe, zencodecs or a pixel decoder.

The default build supports metadata/EXIF filtering and serialization, plus
rendering-preserving retention for an already parsed ISO gain map. Optional `xmp` and `audit` features enable namespace-aware XML
inspection and structural metadata reports independently. `apple` enables
MakerNote and binary-plist inspection without XML or audit. `inventory` enables
the TIFF/BigTIFF walker used with codec-specific consumption rules. All features support
`no_std + alloc`; no unsafe code is used.

```rust
use zencodec::{GainMapParams, Metadata, MetadataPolicy};

let metadata = Metadata::none();
let params = GainMapParams::default();
let retained = zenmeta::display::filter_for_gain_map(
    &metadata, &params, &MetadataPolicy::PreserveExact,
)?;
assert_eq!(retained, metadata);
# Ok::<(), zenmeta::display::Error>(())
```

An audit reports its coverage limits and opaque content. It does not certify
privacy. Container framing, packet reassembly and rewriting belong to codecs;
an inventory is not a safe generic deletion recipe.

See [source provenance](https://github.com/imazen/zencodec/blob/main/zenmeta/PROVENANCE.md) and the workspace
[design](https://github.com/imazen/zencodec/blob/main/docs/zenmeta-design.md).

The `xmp` feature also provides gain-map XMP parsing/generation and Google
container-directory inspection under `zenmeta::xmp::{gainmap, container}`.
JPEG APP framing and packet reassembly remain codec responsibilities.

Optional `rewrite` supplies bounded EXIF processing and fallible plan assembly
for codec-owned rewriters. Requests, services and completed plans are zencodec
types, so a codec need not expose zenmeta types in its public API.

`xmp::container::Directory` validates a complete GContainer packet and updates
secondary lengths by semantic while preserving unrelated source bytes. It
rejects ambiguous directories and missing carried payloads. Codecs still own
MPF offsets, payload layout and APP/box framing.

Basic EXIF reading, orientation, ICC/CICP and ISO gain-map interpretation remain
available in zencodec without zenmeta. New processing callers use
`zenmeta::metadata::filter` and `zenmeta::exif::{filter, retain, serialize}`.
The published zencodec writers are deprecated compatibility implementations;
these entry points delegate to that single implementation until a breaking
release can physically relocate it without a dependency cycle.

Rewrite requests carry policy, services and budgets but do not execute them.
`zenmeta::rewrite::Context::new` performs admission checks; packet processing and
bounded plan assembly also live here. `PreserveExact` can retain XMP without an
editor. Explicit XMP editing still requires a service, and keeping descriptive
bytes does not certify their privacy or make unsupported container edits valid.

Apple iOS MakerNote HDR gain-map metadata extraction.

Apple HEIC/JPEG captures encode their HDR gain-map *headroom* inside the
EXIF MakerNote (TIFF tag `0x927C`), **not** in XMP — the embedded gain-map
image's XMP carries only `HDRGainMapVersion`. The headroom is derived from
two Apple MakerNote tags, per exiftool's `Image::ExifTool::Apple`:

| Tag      | Name          | Type          | Role             |
|----------|---------------|---------------|------------------|
| `0x0021` | `HDRHeadroom` | `rational64s` | "maker33"        |
| `0x0030` | `HDRGain`     | `rational64s` | "maker48"        |
| `0x000A` | `HDRImageType`| `int32s`      | 3 = HDR, 4 = SDR |

The headroom (in stops, i.e. log2 luminance ratio) is computed from
`maker33` and `maker48` with the community/Apple-derived piecewise formula
(see [`AppleHdrInfo::headroom_stops`]). The exact constants are not in a
published Apple specification; final fidelity is validated by the gain-map
round-trip test, not asserted to be bit-exact here.

References:
- exiftool `lib/Image/ExifTool/Apple.pm`
- <https://juniperphoton.substack.com/p/decoding-some-hidden-magic-of-makerapple>
- <https://photoinvestigator.co/blog/the-mystery-of-maker-apple-metadata/>

This module is pure byte parsing: `no_std` + `alloc`, no transcendental
math, zero new dependencies. The IFD-walk mechanics mirror the proven
reader in `zenraw::apple`, with the corrected exiftool tag IDs.

`0x30 HDRGain` ("maker48"). Defaults to `0.0` when the tag is absent
(Apple omits it on many captures; the formula treats absent as zero).

`0x21 HDRHeadroom` ("maker33"). `None` when the tag is absent — which
means there is no Apple HDR gain-map signal at all.
`0x0a HDRImageType`: `Some(3)` = HDR Image, `Some(4)` = Original/SDR.

HDR headroom in **stops** (log2 luminance ratio), or `None` when no

Piecewise mapping of `maker33` (`HDRHeadroom`) and `maker48`
(`HDRGain`), clamped to be non-negative:

```text
if maker33 < 1:  stops = maker48 <= 0.01 ? -20·maker48 + 1.8  : -0.101·maker48 + 1.601
else:            stops = maker48 <= 0.01 ? -70·maker48 + 3.0  : -0.44 ·maker48 + 2.86
stops = max(stops, 0)
```

The base image is SDR (`base_hdr_headroom = 0`); the alternate (HDR)
headroom is the computed stops value (already log2-domain, matching
`GainMapParams`). Per-channel gain spans `[0, stops]` in log2 with unit
gamma — the Apple convention where the `[0,1]` gain-map image scales
luminance from SDR up to the headroom. Returns `None` when no `0x21`
headroom tag is present.

**Note:** the per-channel curve is the documented Apple convention; the
gain-map round-trip test is the authority on fidelity.

Parse an Apple iOS MakerNote blob (`"Apple iOS\0"` + version + byte-order

Addressing has two bases (verified against iPhone 8/13/16/17 captures):
the byte-order marker and IFD live at offset 12, but the entries' *value
offsets* for out-of-line data are relative to the MakerNote start
(`maker[0]`). Unrecognized notes, malformed entries or duplicate rendering
tags refuse extraction. The inspection view reports malformed entries individually.

Minimal Apple binary property list (`bplist00`) reader.

Several Apple MakerNote tags (e.g. `RunTime`, auto-exposure state) store an
embedded `bplist00` blob rather than a plain TIFF value. This reader decodes
the common object types well enough to inspect those structures. It is a
reader only — there is no writer — and it is deliberately small.

Format reference: CoreFoundation `CFBinaryPList` (`bplist00`):
8-byte `"bplist00"` header, packed objects, an offset table, and a 32-byte
trailer giving the integer widths, object count, top object index, and the
offset-table location.

`no_std` + `alloc`, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Recursion is depth-bounded so
a maliciously cyclic ref graph cannot blow the stack.

Crate-agnostic TIFF structure walk for structural inventories.

Shared by `zentiff` and `zenraw`; each supplies its decoder rules.
The walk parses a TIFF header, every IFD reachable from the IFD
chain and from pointer entries, out-of-line values and the extents
(strips, tiles, free space, JPEG streams) the directories reference. A
crate supplies [`Rules`] saying what its decode path does with each piece;
the walk never decodes pixels.

TIFF parts can interleave in any order, so a TIFF's parts are siblings in
file order: header, IFDs (each with one child `Field` per entry),
out-of-line values (`Field`, same tag as their entry) and extents.
Where parts overlap, each byte takes the strongest fate among the parts
covering it ([`Placed`]); the others are split around it, with a note in
both details. Nothing overlapping is ever emitted.

XMP serialization for Ultra HDR and related multi-image JPEG formats.

This module handles the Adobe/Google XMP metadata used by Ultra HDR:

- `hdrgm:*` namespace — gain-map numerical parameters (min, max,
  gamma, offsets, HDR headroom). Generated by [`generate_xmp`] and
  friends; parsed by [`parse_xmp`].
- `Container:Directory` — GContainer item manifest used by Google
  Camera and Android Dynamic Depth Format. Emitted by
  [`generate_xmp_with_items`]; parsed alongside metadata by
  [`parse_xmp_full`]. See [`super::container`] for `ContainerItem` and
  `ItemSemantic`.

Upper bound on XMP packet length accepted by [`parse_xmp`]. Guards
against CPU exhaustion on crafted inputs.

Matches `ultrahdr_core::limits::MAX_XMP_LENGTH` (the pre-migration
value) so callers moving between the old and new API see no change
in accepted input size. Legitimate gain-map XMP is well under
32 KB, but Extended XMP reassembly + base64-encoded depth-map
payloads (GDepth / Android Dynamic Depth) can push into MB range,
so a generous cap is appropriate.

Goes in the gain-map JPEG's APP1 marker. Together with the primary's
`Container:Directory` XMP, this matches libultrahdr's canonical

Generate XMP for the primary JPEG: `Container:Directory` only.

The primary image's XMP contains `hdrgm:Version` and the
`Container:Directory` listing every secondary with its semantic and
byte length. The numeric gain-map metadata goes in the secondary's
XMP via [`generate_gainmap_xmp`]. This matches the layout produced
by Google Camera / Android.
